<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

<!-- Summarize the change in 1-2 lines. Link relevant issues and PRs. -->

Add opt-in `vllm run-batch --output-order completion` so finished responses reach the output file without waiting for an earlier slow request. Input order remains the default.

Related to #60184. This is separate from #62895, which resumes records already on disk and explicitly leaves cancellation and write-order behavior unchanged. The proposed scope was explained in [the issue discussion](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60184#issuecomment-6528693500).

## Claims

<!-- State the accomplishments in a few concrete bullets: speedups, feature support, bug fixes, etc. -->

- Preserve the current input-order default; completion order is explicitly selected.
- Flush each finished response immediately in completion mode, keeping the existing in-flight limit, error handling, and cancellation cleanup.
- Document matching by `custom_id`, safe retries to a different file, and the unchanged upload-on-success behavior for URL outputs.

## Validation

<!-- Show evidence that the claims are met by this change, and steps to reproduce validations. -->

Validated on Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64 under WSL, Python 3.12.3, and PyTorch 2.14.0+cpu. Tests use actual `hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM` weights for the CLI runs.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Initial regressions with original production code at `e811e502` | 7 failed, 10 passed; the new CLI option and dispatcher argument are unsupported |
| Dispatcher, writer, both real CLI output modes, and upstream response regressions on `69d27bf8` | 21 passed, 50 deselected |
| Real CPU CLI interrupted with SIGINT | Both fast results were on disk before and after interruption; the first slow request was still pending |
| Full configured Linux pre-commit | Passed, including Ruff, Markdown lint, configured mypy, SPDX, and Buildkite test tethering; no forced skips |
| Independent production-module Python 3.11 type check | Passed |

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands and interruption evidence</summary>

With the CPU environment active, from the source checkout:

```bash
# Initial baseline at e811e502: original production module plus the new tests.
# Result: 7 failed, 10 passed.
VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0 VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=1 VLLM_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND=nobind \
uv run --active --no-project python -m pytest \
  --confcutdir=tests/entrypoints/launchers \
  tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_run_batch.py \
  -k "dispatch or output_writer or (completions_endpoint and True)" -q

# Integrated source at 69d27bf8, including the unchanged default CLI mode.
# Result: 21 passed, 50 deselected.
VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0 VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=1 VLLM_CPU_OMP_THREADS_BIND=nobind \
uv run --active --no-project python -m pytest \
  --confcutdir=tests/entrypoints/launchers \
  tests/entrypoints/launchers/test_run_batch.py \
  -k "dispatch or output_writer or completions_endpoint or batch_embedding_json_responses or batch_rejects_json_stream" -q

# Passed.
uv run --active --no-project pre-commit run

# Passed.
uv run --active --no-project mypy --python-version 3.11 --platform linux \
  --follow-imports silent vllm/entrypoints/launchers/run_batch.py
```

The SIGINT smoke used one 1,024-token request followed by two short requests, with `--max-inflight 3 --output-order completion --enforce-eager`. It waited for complete successful JSONL records before sending SIGINT:

```text
Before interrupt: ['fast-1', 'fast-2']
After interrupt: ['fast-1', 'fast-2']
CLI return code: -2
PASS: real CPU inference results survived CLI interruption
```

</details>

Initial validation used Python sources based on `e811e502`. Before submission, the feature was applied to current upstream at `69d27bf8002a4634de1699c95fb0aeb22fb86ca5`, retaining the upstream embedding-response fix and resolving only an overlapping test import. The CPU suite and configured hooks were rerun on that integrated source.

Native extensions come from the published official CPU wheel at `335dd77b09161c5d63139b4e7ae51bb9928305b1`, installed with the documented precompiled editable workflow and an explicit wheel location. Recent per-commit CPU wheels were unavailable during setup. These checks validate the Python changes with that CPU runtime, not a fresh native build of the source commit. The original Windows-authored and Linux-tested patches were compared byte-for-byte before integration.

No CUDA, other model families, or general serving-performance evaluation is claimed. The repository-configured type-check hook passes.

Upstream [pre-commit CI](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/41841103870/job/126612643431) is currently stopped by the contributor-eligibility gate. The [docs build](https://app.readthedocs.org/api/v2/build/35643254.txt) stops at that prerequisite, before MkDocs runs. These are separate from the passing local checks above.

## Details

<!-- Explain motivation, design decisions, root cause, tradeoffs, and limitations concisely. Link or collapse lengthy supporting material. -->

In input-order mode, a slow early request can hold already-finished responses in the reorder buffer. An interrupted run loses those unwritten responses. Completion mode avoids that buffer: each response is written and flushed when its request finishes. Cancelled work still produces no additional output, and a dead engine still stops dispatch.

The change is deliberately opt-in. Consumers of completion-order output must use unique `custom_id` values instead of line positions. A partial output is not necessarily an input prefix. This does not add automatic resume, retries, or stronger filesystem durability guarantees. URL outputs remain staged and are uploaded only after the whole batch succeeds.

The tests reuse the existing launcher suite, add event-controlled real handlers and files, cover in-flight bounds and progress in both modes, and extend the existing real CLI routing test. The existing Entrypoints Unit Buildkite lane selects this test file.

Duplicate checks inspected the current #60184 discussion, #62895's explicit scope, and open PR searches for batch ordering, completion order, flushing, and cancellation. A contributor had offered a related shutdown-flush follow-up; the coordination note explains this different opt-in design and offers to step back if it overlaps.

- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.

 Run batch prompts and write results to file.
 
+Responses are written in input order by default. Use `--output-order completion`
+to write each response as soon as it finishes, without waiting for earlier
+requests. Match results to inputs using `custom_id`, not line position. An
+interrupted local output file in this mode is not necessarily an input prefix;
+filter completed IDs rather than skipping the same number of input lines.
+Use a different output file for retries, since a new run truncates its output.
+Output URLs are still uploaded only after the whole batch succeeds.
+
 Running with a local file:
 
 ```bash

@@ -77,6 +77,28 @@ complete. To resume, rerun the input lines past the last one written; if the
 process was killed, drop a final line that is incomplete first. An output URL is
 uploaded only when the run succeeds.
 
+To avoid holding finished responses behind an earlier slow request, opt into
+completion-order output:
+
+```bash
+vllm run-batch \
+    -i examples/features/openai_batch/openai_example_batch.jsonl \
+    -o results.jsonl \
+    --model meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct \
+    --output-order completion
+```
+
+In this mode, each finished response is written immediately. Responses already
+written to a local file remain available if another request fails or the run is
+cancelled. Match them by `custom_id`: their line positions do not correspond to
+the input, and a partial output is not necessarily an input prefix. Each input
+request must have a unique `custom_id`. To continue
+an interrupted job, filter the input by completed successful IDs rather than
+skipping an equal number of lines, and write retries to a different output file
+so the existing results are not overwritten. This option does not implement automatic
+resume or retry. A process killed during a write can still leave an incomplete
+final line, and output URLs are still uploaded only when the run succeeds.
